newsitem.title: USA: Members named to accounting standards board.
newsitem.headline: Members named to accounting standards board.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission and the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants Monday jointly named eight people to a new board created to set improved standards for independent auditors.
The Independence Standards Board is made up of corporate executives with accounting backgrounds and heads of some of America's leading accounting firms.
The board, chaired by Chancellor William Allen of the Delaware Chancery Court, is expected to convene for the first time in July, at which time an executive director will be named.

"Success in clarifying which auditor activities are consistent with the integrity of audited financial statements can contribute to the reliability of financial data and promote informed, efficient capital markets," Allen said.
The board was created in response to rising challenges of addressing auditor independence issues as business and professional relationships have become more complex.

In addition to Allen, the board's members include Vanguard Group Inc. Chairman John Bogel, Salomon Inc. Chairman Robert Denham and Manuel Johnson, co-chairman and senior partner of Johnson Smick International and former vice chairman of the board of governors of the Federal Reserve.

The accounting profession members are KPMG Peat Marwick LLP Chairman Stephen Butler, Ernst & Young LLP Chairman Philip Laskawy, institute president Barry Melancon and Price Waterhouse LLP President James Schiro.
